title_en: 351 Conversions: Smart Tax Alpha Strategy or Loophole in the Code?
title_zh: 351 转换：聪明的税收阿尔法策略，还是税法里的漏洞？
subtitle_zh: Bloomberg News 记者拆解超级富豪用定制 ETF 递延巨额资本利得税的玩法：从 Hot Pockets 家族到 Treasury 划出的监管红线。
summary_zh: Joe Weber 与 Eric Balchunas 请来 Bloomberg News 记者 Deniza Petrova 与 Zachary Mider，聊报道《超级富豪最新的避税手段是一只定制化 ETF》揭示的 351 转换。Eric 解释 ETF 的税务优势：券商账户卖出即缴资本利得税，而 ETF 除非持有人卖出一般不派发资本利得；如今更有人用 351 交换把高度集中的持仓（如 Nvidia）换成分散化 ETF，递延纳税，甚至靠继承时的计税基础递增彻底免税。Deniza 指出该条款已存在一个多世纪，原为把资产投入公司换股份而设计，2019 年 ETF 规则改革使其更易套用；Zach 认为这是不同时期的规则被组合出制定者未曾设想的结果。两人已识别 105 只此类 ETF、资产超 200 亿美元，案例包括注资超 5 亿美元的 Merage（Hot Pockets）家族、自称最早操盘的 Rory Riggs 与 GameStop 事件中的 Gabe Plotkin，并谈到分摊成本的辛迪加模式与更早的昂贵版本交换基金。监管方面，Treasury 官员表示无意打击全部 351，但反对 stuffing（借钱塞资产绕过分散化规则）与 sequential seeding 等激进做法；业内最担心此类交易被列为「关注交易」而遭 IRS 重点审查，且更可能以指引而非国会立法处理。节目还讨论了 tax alpha 的商业逻辑、投顾为收费合理性推销节税，以及股市财富差距议题。
description: 351 Conversions: Smart Tax Alpha Strategy or Loophole in the Code?

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios, podcasts, radio news, Bokerhillions.
turns.zh: Bloomberg Audio Studios，播客、广播、新闻，Bloomberg Trillions。

turns.en: I'm Joel Webber and I'm Eric Belchernas.
turns.zh: 我是 Joe Weber，我是 Eric Balchunas。

turns.en: Nobody likes to pay taxes, but some people are really good about reducing their liabilities. And that's a thing about ETFs. They have some tax efficiencies. Shall we say, what is it about ETFs that make them so special? In the text front?
turns.zh: 没人喜欢交税，但有些人在减少税负方面确实非常在行。而这正是 ETF 的一个特点——它们在税务上有一定的效率优势。那么，ETF 在税务方面究竟有什么特别之处？

turns.en: This is one of the big attributes because if you're in a four one K plan, you're already tax deferred, so you're loving life. But if you're outside of a four wing K plan in a brokerage account, taxes are pain because every time you sell, you got to pay tax on the capital gains. And you still do that with ETFs. But what ETFs do that, especially as better of the mutual funds, is they generally don't distribute capital gains distributions unless you sell, so I actually think they're taxed more properly. Mutual funds, on their hand, are unfortunate in that whenever they sell, they have to cash somebody out and that triggers the capital gains and the people in the fund then are hit with a tax bill. So that's why mutual funds a huge reason why especially advisors really love ETFs. They just hate getting a tax bill when they didn't do anything. Now that I think that's the fair way to get taxed. However, there's a new evolution and even a wing of the ETF market that's evolving using the ETF for even more tax deferral. So this is a three point fifty one exchange. It's ETFs that are sort of custom made or bespoke for somebody to sort of take big gains in a stock they have and they and the stock has kind of taken over their portfolio, and they can move it into the ETF with a diversified basket of securities and defer paying taxes on it in effort to diversify their portfolio. And this is a trend that's growing. There's about eighty five to ninety of these now, and especially in the last year or two, they have about eighteen billions, So they're not big, but they're a pound for pound growing very quickly. And there's people who specialize in helping clients do this. And you know, if you talk to an advisor, you know, rich people almost tay paying taxes more than they like good returns. I mean, it's like they hate it. So obviously there's a lot of demand for this, and it's a questionable whether it is an abuse of the tax code or just an interpretation. And so I think that's what we're going to discuss today.
turns.zh: 这是 ETF 的一大优势。因为如果你在 401(k) 计划里，你本来就是递延纳税的，日子过得很舒服。但如果你的钱在 401(k) 之外、放在券商账户里，税就很让人头疼：每次卖出，你都得为资本利得缴税。买 ETF 卖出时同样要缴。但 ETF 相比共同基金更好的一点是，除非你自己卖出，否则它一般不会派发资本利得分配（capital gains distribution），所以我其实认为 ETF 的征税方式更合理。共同基金就比较不幸：只要基金卖出资产，就得把某人兑现离场，这会触发资本利得，于是基金里的持有人被砸下一张税单。这也是为什么——尤其是投顾——特别喜欢 ETF 的一大原因：他们讨厌自己什么都没做却收到税单。我也认为这才是公平的征税方式。不过，现在出现了一种新的演进，ETF 市场里甚至有一个分支正在发展，用 ETF 实现更多的税收递延。这就是 351 交换（Section 351 exchange）。这类 ETF 是为某个人量身定制的：他手上某只股票涨了很多、已经在组合里占了过大比重，于是他把这些股票转入一只持有分散证券篮子的 ETF，从而在分散组合的同时递延缴税。这个趋势还在增长。现在大约有 85 到 90 只这样的 ETF，尤其是一两年内出现的，管理规模约 180 亿美元。所以体量不大，但按同等规模看增长非常快。而且已经有人专门帮客户做这件事。你要跟投顾聊就知道，富人讨厌交税的程度几乎超过他们喜欢好回报的程度，他们是真心厌恶交税。所以这类需求显然很大。而它到底是对税法的滥用，还是只是一种解释，是有争议的。我想这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

turns.en: Because there was a recent story from Bloomberg News called headline the latest tax dodge for the ultra rich is a customized ETF and there was a group of reporters on that, two of whom are joining us today, Deniza Takova and Zacharymeider, and we're going to just gus the three fifty one conversion with them, this time on trillions tax dodge. Denita, Zach what can aw trillions?
turns.zh: 因为 Bloomberg News 最近有一篇报道，标题是《超级富豪最新的避税手段是一只定制化 ETF》，署名是一组记者，其中两位今天来到节目——Deniza Petrova 和 Zachary Mider，我们要和他们一起深入聊聊 351 转换，这就是本期 Trillions 的主题：避税（tax dodge）。Deniza、Zach，欢迎做客 Trillions。

turns.en: Thanks for having us.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我们。

turns.en: It's great to be here.
turns.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

turns.en: So one person who I was hoping to join is Justin Alis. She's in London. We were unable to include her. She's the lead byline on this story, So shout out to Justina for all of her reporting. Denis, I'm going to start with you, what is this three to fifty one conversion that we just talked about?
turns.zh: 本来我还希望另一位记者能来，Justina Lee，但她在伦敦，我们没能把她接入。她是这篇报道的第一署名，所以要特别感谢 Justina 的全部采访工作。Deniza，我先从你开始：我们刚才说的这个 351 转换到底是什么？

turns.en: So three fifty one conversions existed in a tax code for more than a century. It's been something that's been around for a very long time. What you can use it for is to transfer property to a corporation in exchange for shares. It's been used very differently in the ATF. There was a big ETF rout change in twenty nineteen. We've talked about it in many different things like leverage gtfs and other products, but it made it easier for that conversion to be part of a ETF. And what happens is that if I have a very concentrated portfolio, if I've invested all in magnificent seven, if it's most of my portfolio, and I want to diversify some of those gains, some people have been going to three fifty one conversions and they've been swapping parts of the portfolio after they become an ETF to replace some of the holdings with the goal to have a tax deferral, but also the potential to ultimately avoid taxes if, for example, those gains are passed onto the next generation through step up.
turns.zh: 351 转换在税法里已经存在一个多世纪了，是一项由来已久的规定。它的用途是把财产转让给一家公司，以换取该公司的股份。而在 ETF 领域，它的用法非常不同。2019 年 ETF 规则发生了重大变化——我们在杠杆 ETF 等很多话题上都谈过——那次变化让 351 转换更容易成为 ETF 的一部分。情况是这样的：如果我有一个非常集中的组合，比如我全押在 Magnificent Seven 上、它占了组合的大头，而我想把其中一些收益分散掉，那么有些人就会去做 351 转换。他们在资产变成 ETF 之后，把组合的一部分换掉、替换成其他持仓，目的是实现税收递延，而且最终还有可能彻底避税——比如通过计税基础递增（step-up in basis）把这些收益传给下一代。

turns.en: Basis, Zach, isn't this the tax code's fault?
turns.zh: 计税基础（basis）。Zach，这难道不是税法本身的错吗？

turns.en: Well, you're assuming there's a problem, yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯，你这前提是先假定这里有问题。

turns.en: Exactly, But what is it about the tax one hundred years? Like, what is the loophole that suddenly exists here?
turns.zh: 对，但税法已经存在一百年了，问题出在哪儿？这里突然冒出来的漏洞到底是什么？

turns.en: So as with as always a case with tax what happens is you you have different rules that were conceived for different purposes at different times that now people are kind of finding new ways to use to work together to get results that no one would have contemplated back when they created the rules in the first place. So the three fifty one conversion thing, the idea was like, if I own a bunch of of you know, machines, and I want to create a corporation to like, you know, own the widget factory, I can contribute these assets in exchange for stock in the corporation without having to have a tax realization event. Totally makes sense, not what we're talking about here. Then ETFs have this magical ability, which I'm sure we've talked about many times. They have a magical ability to be able to sort of get rid of assets and get new ones without incurring a capital gain. And so when you combine these two things together, you have this like amazing opportunity which is like I've got some video and video stock. It went way up. If I sold it, I would have to pay a lot of tax. Maybe I can just stick it in an ETF, have the ETF sell it and in exchange for something else I want to own, and I can just put off paying a tax bill for some indefinite amount of time.
turns.zh: 跟税务领域一贯的情况一样：不同的规则是在不同时期、为不同目的而设计的，如今人们找到了新的用法，把它们组合起来，得到当年制定规则的人根本不会想到的结果。351 转换原本的设想是：假如我拥有一堆机器，想成立一家公司来经营这个小部件工厂，我可以把这些资产投入公司换取股份，而不必触发一次应税的实现事件。这完全说得通，但这不是我们今天要谈的东西。而 ETF 有一种神奇的能力——我相信我们讲过很多次——它可以把资产换掉、换入新资产，却不产生资本利得。把这两件事结合在一起，就出现了一个绝妙的机会：我手上有一些 Nvidia 股票，涨了很多；如果我卖掉，就得缴一大笔税。那也许我可以把它塞进一只 ETF，让 ETF 把它卖掉、换成我真正想持有的东西，这样我就可以把税单无限期地往后推。

turns.en: Eric, when did you first hear about three fifty one conversions.
turns.zh: Eric，你最早是什么时候听说 351 转换的？

turns.en: Three years ago?
turns.zh: 三年前？

turns.en: Maybe?
turns.zh: 也许吧？

turns.en: I mean they've been around. I think the first one was twenty nineteen, twenty twenty. But there's a lot of ETFs now that pop up that came from somewhere else, like some separate managed Some advisors just convert a separate account into an ETF. It's hard to tell that it's a three fifty one. They don't have like some new thing. A lot of times, if it's a name that's like sounds like I don't know, some fancy pants advisor like Clearbridge or something, I'm like, Okay, that's probably a three point fifty one. Whereas if it's something like you know, Parlay Shares, that's probably a legit you know, issuer launching new digen leverage products, you know. Like So generally, when I see a name like that, I'm like, Okay, that's probably some kind of a person sitting on something that wants to use the ETF. First of all, if you put your Navidia shares into this three fifty one, and all of a sudden you're now in a diversified portfolio, which again I think technically is the law allows, although spiritually, as you said, it was more for small businesses. If you do that and then you sell that fun, say in ten years, you are still paying a tax based on when you've bought Navidia. So in that regard, you are I say, dodging paying tax at the time that you want to get rid of Navidia, but you're not dodging it completely. Is that right?
turns.zh: 我是说它们已经存在一阵子了，我想第一只出现在 2019 或 2020 年。但现在有很多新冒出来的 ETF 其实来自别处，比如某个独立管理账户——有些投顾就是把一个独立账户直接转成 ETF。你很难看出它是一个 351，它们并没有打上什么新标签。很多时候，如果基金名字听起来像是——我不知道——某个花哨的投顾，比如 ClearBridge 之类，我就会想：好吧，那多半是个 351。而如果名字像 Parlay Shares 那种，那大概率是一家正经发行商在推新的杠杆类产品。所以一般来说，看到那种名字，我就会想：那大概是某个人手上压着一堆资产，想借 ETF 来处理。首先，如果你把 Nvidia 股份放进这个 351，突然间你就处在一个分散化的组合里了——我认为这在技术上确实是法律允许的，尽管从立法精神上讲，正如你说的，它更多是为小企业设计的。如果你这么做，然后在比如十年后卖掉那只基金，你缴税的依据仍然是你当初买入 Nvidia 的时间点。所以从这个角度看，你算是躲过了在你想脱手 Nvidia 那一刻要缴的税，但你并没有完全躲掉。对吧？

turns.en: Oh? That's absolutely right?
turns.zh: 对，完全正确。

turns.en: So how far can you kick the tax can down the road.
turns.zh: 那么，这个税罐子最远能被往后踢到什么时候？

turns.en: When you're talking about three fifty ones? To set up a whole ETF, it's kind of a big deal. If you've got ten thousand dollars of gains from playing around in the stock market, you cannot afford to create your own custom ETF to lay off some of those gains. This works really well if you have one hundred million dollars worth of of stock.
turns.zh: 说到 351：要设立一整只 ETF 是件挺大的事。如果你在股市里炒出了 1 万美元的收益，你根本负担不起为自己定制一只 ETF 来卸掉部分收益。但如果你有 1 亿美元的股票，这个办法就非常好用。

turns.en: Is there a number in between those two numbers that I might inspire too?
turns.zh: 在这两个数字之间，有没有一个我可以朝着努力的门槛？

turns.en: So some of these deals are like one guy or a couple families. Some are more syndicated. You round up a whole bunch of people with like a million dollars worth of stock each. So either way though, we're talking about people who are a fairly decent money.
turns.zh: 有些这类交易就是一个人或者几个家庭。有些则更偏辛迪加（syndicated）模式：你召集一大批人，每人持有大约 100 万美元的股票。但不管是哪种，我们说的都是手上有相当一笔钱的人。

turns.en: Yeah. Give us an example, Danitza from the story, who is one of the most noteworthy examples.
turns.zh: 好。Deniza，给我们举个例子：报道里谁是最值得关注的案例之一？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: So we start with the hot Pocket family, the Mirage family.
turns.zh: 那我们就从 Hot Pockets 家族——Merage 家族说起。

turns.en: Pocket as in the Snack.
turns.zh: Hot Pockets，就是那个零食。

turns.en: As in the Snack, it's a as far as we know, billionaire family that did their own three fifty one conversion. It was more than five hundred million that was seeded with We know that the majority pockets. Yeah, we know that the majority of that money comes from the family. We've reported also on Gabe Podkin, which was obviously a well known named part of the game Stop Saga with his hedge funds. Eric was talking about the first three fifty one conversions. We actually speak to Rory Riggs who says that he was the first one to do it. Obviously it's kind of hard to define, but he did it I think twenty eighteen, twenty nineteen. What he said at the time it was very vague, very confusing. He actually ensured the three fifty one conversions. Most of the conversions now are not really insured because I guess it's a pretty straight forward procedure. By the time, it was very unclear. He said that actually the insurer came to him and he was like, let's do this. So he has four ETFs like that that are done with Syntex advisors. That's something that Eric also said. A lot of those ETFs you can find the name of the advisors, and it's like, that's clearly something normal people don't really do in a ETF filing. But he did four of those ETFs, and he puts some of his money in each of those. But then he worked with other investors and client of his to see that DF as well.
turns.zh: 就是那个零食。据我们所知，这是一个亿万富翁家族，他们做了自己的 351 转换。初始注入的资金超过 5 亿美元，我们知道其中大部分钱来自这个家族。我们还报道过 Gabe Plotkin——他的对冲基金在 GameStop 事件中显然是个家喻户晓的名字。Eric 刚才说到最早的几笔 351 转换，我们确实采访了 Rory Riggs，他说自己才是第一个做这件事的人。当然这很难界定，但我想他是在 2018 或 2019 年做的。他当时说，情况非常模糊、非常让人困惑——他真的为这笔 351 转换买了保险。而现在大多数转换其实并不投保，因为我想这个流程已经相当直接了。当时很不明确，他说是保险公司主动找上门，然后他就说：那就干吧。他有四只这样的 ETF，是和 Syntex Advisors 一起做的。Eric 也提到过这一点：很多这类 ETF 的申报文件里你能看到投顾的名字，而这显然不是普通人在 ETF 备案中会出现的东西。他做了四只这样的 ETF，每一只里都放了一些自己的钱，然后又和其他投资者、他的客户一起为这些 ETF 注入种子资金。

turns.en: Eric. The name of the ETF is the m ig meg Core ETF. The ticker is Migo. When you look at Migo, what do you see Because this is a new ETF. Right when we talked about this, a little bit like with that one, I've even crossed your radar. It sounds so inoquous. It's just like Migo. There seems like there could be a million different ETFs that had that name.
turns.zh: Eric，这只 ETF 的名字是 MIG Core ETF，代码是 MIGO。你看 MIGO 的时候看到的是什么？因为这是一只新 ETF，我们刚聊到这个话题时它甚至都没进入你的雷达。这个名字听起来太无害了，就叫 MIGO，感觉有一百万只不同的 ETF 都可以叫这个名字。

turns.en: I remember seeing it and I got to be honest, you know, as a kid raised on movies and TV in the eighties, it says meg corn. I thought of top Gun. There's also a top Gun ETF, by the way, that is a legit active fund. Maybe this is like somebody using the word meg as like a metaphor for active. Either way, what I assume is it's one of these conversions like an advisor, or it's somebody who's working with a white label issuer and they're too small to like run their own ETF, because if you look at like title or ETF architect or exchange trait of concepts and you look at their lineups, it's a bunch of really small names you never heard of, and so I would just put it in that category, but I wouldn't have there's nothing to say that it's at three fifty one. If you look at the holdings, it's very diversified. It holds fifty stocks. Well, actually two of them are ets owns VU the cues, and then a bunch of stocks like Google, Microsoft, Blackstone, Eli, Lilly. Kind of looks like kind of a mix between maybe like a advisor account, you know, because you've got two ETFs and then a bunch of stocks. This is probably not the kind of fun where you're going to see a lot of inflows. Because it's not really trying to do anything. I don't think it's marketing itself, and so looks like the only inflows that have happened have been like heartbeat trades, which are probably trying to do something with the games that are embedded there. You know, it is up a little bit. So yeah, that's my initial thought. But again there's no tag on it that says it's a three fifty one exchange.
turns.zh: 我记得看到过它。说实话，作为一个在八十年代电影电视里长大的人，一看到 MIG Core，我就想到了 Top Gun。顺便说一句，还真有一只 Top Gun ETF，是只正经的主动管理基金。也许这是有人拿 MIG 这个词当作主动管理的隐喻。不管怎样，我的推测是：它属于这类转换之一，来自某家投顾，或者是有人和一家白标发行商合作、规模太小而没法自己运营一只 ETF。因为如果你去看 Tuttle、ETF Architect 或者 Exchange Traded Concepts 这些平台的产品阵容，里面全是一堆你从没听说过的小名字。所以我会把它归到那一类，但我原本不会想到——因为没有任何标注说明它是一个 351。如果你看它的持仓，非常分散，持有 50 只标的。嗯，实际上其中两个是 ETF——它持有 QQQ——然后是一堆股票，比如 Google、Microsoft、Blackstone、Eli Lilly。看起来有点像投顾账户的组合，因为你有两只 ETF，再加一堆个股。这大概不会是那种会有大量资金流入的基金，因为它其实并不想做什么，我认为它也没在做营销。所以看起来唯一发生过的流入就是所谓的心跳交易（heartbeat trade），那大概是想处理里面嵌着的收益。它确实涨了一点。嗯，这就是我最初的想法。但同样，它身上没有任何标签说明这是一笔 351 交换。

turns.en: What would happen if I tried to buy a share of Migo?
turns.zh: 如果我想买一股 MIGO，会发生什么？

turns.en: You would buy a share Amigo. I mean, if I look at the volume, it's really pathetic. This thing barely trades even though it has seven hundred million. In fact, the volume per asset to this has probably got to be one of the widest margins I've ever seen. Like, let's just say, like on Monday, it traded six hundred and ninety one shares. I mean, that's that's like nothing. I think, you're not even like, if you trade like less than a million shares a day, you're struggling. So six hundred and ninety one is really really bad. However, every now and then it sees a day with a million or two. That's clearly not a real flow. That's a purposeful inkind redemption, and that would be a heartbeat trade. So I guess the lego people don't. It doesn't matter, Like if somebody were to buy this, like you eat fine, you know the ats very very well. It's you know, standardized and durable and easy to use for anybody, and you don't have to use it, like if you bought it or not, it wouldn't matter. It can still live on and just be for this one person and.
turns.zh: 你就真能买到一股 MIGO。我是说，如果我看它的成交量，真的很可怜。这只基金有 7 亿美元资产，却几乎不交易。事实上，它的成交量与资产之比，可能是我见过的最悬殊的之一。比如说，周一它只成交了 691 股。这基本上等于没有量。我觉得，就算一天成交不到 100 万股，你都算很挣扎了，所以 691 股真的是非常非常糟糕。不过每隔一段时间，它会出现一天成交一两百万股的情况。那显然不是真实资金流，而是有目的的实物赎回（in-kind redemption），也就是心跳交易。所以我猜，持有人那边也不在意这件事。如果有人真买了这只 ETF——你们这些 ETF 老手都很清楚——ETF 这个结构非常标准化、耐用，对任何人都易于使用，而且你不一定非得用它。所以买不买都没关系，它照样能存活下去，就只服务这一个人。

turns.en: For this one person or this family for instance. What's their end game, whether the various scenarios that this could take from here.
turns.zh: 就以这一个人、或者这个家庭为例，他们的终局是什么？从这里往后可能出现哪些不同的情形？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean the first thing because Eric said, oh eventually, maybe not everyone wants to pass this. Maybe it's no step up basis, but they're versifying your position without realizing taxes is a pretty good benefit. It gives me the flexibility to talk to do a lot of tax planning, like maybe I want to realize the games, but maybe I want to realize it at my home pace at the right time when I have particular losses. To Job said, you know, we talk a lot about tax alpha, but there are so many sophisticated techniques that you can use to do that right now, so I don't know. Tax engineering has evolved a lot, so having the timing and flexibility to that is great. And you know that's another major benefit that I think gets lost.
turns.zh: 嗯，我是说，第一点：因为 Eric 说过，也许最终并不是每个人都想把资产传下去，也许没有计税基础递增（step-up in basis），但在不实现应税收益的情况下分散你的持仓，本身就是相当大的好处。它给了你做大量税务规划的灵活性：也许我想实现收益，但我想按自己的节奏、在合适的时机、在我有特定亏损可以抵扣的时候去实现。就像 Joe 说的，我们经常谈税收阿尔法（tax alpha），而现在有太多复杂精细的技术可以做到这一点，所以——怎么说呢，税务工程（tax engineering）已经演进了很多，能掌握时机和灵活性是很棒的。我认为这是另一个常常被忽略的重大好处。

turns.en: You just use the phrase tax alfo. Can you break that down, Like what does that mean to you?
turns.zh: 你刚用了 tax alpha 这个词。能拆解一下吗？对你来说它是什么意思？

turns.en: Yeah?

In the industry, Yeah, tax alpha is financial strategies that are aimed at minimizing your tax bill. Of course, they aim at also delivering strong returns, but the returns they focus it's after tax returns. So they were like, yeah, we can deliver you gains, but you're after tax gains will look extra good. And they're like long short tax aware strategies, which is kind of the evolution of direct indexing and SMAs. They're exchange funds. There's so many different tools that over the past decade or so have really lowered minimums, and that's argument people make. Indeed, a lot of high where the individuals can reach them now, a lot of retail folks can reach them now, So those strategies are really optimizing your tax bill in the end.
turns.zh: 在业内，tax alpha 指的是那些以最小化你的税单为目标的金融策略。当然，它们同时也追求强劲的回报，但关注的是税后回报。所以他们会说：没错，我们能给你带来收益，而且你的税后收益会格外漂亮。这类策略包括多空税务敏感策略（long/short tax-aware），算是直接指数化（direct indexing）和独立管理账户（SMA）的演进版本；还有交换基金（exchange fund）。过去十年左右出现了非常多的工具，大幅降低了投资门槛——这也是人们常提的论点：很多高净值个人现在能用到这些，很多散户也能用到了。所以这些策略归根结底是在优化你的税单。

turns.en: Okay, so we talked about how there could be millions of dollars. Maybe one family that has an excess of five hundred million dollars. That does this Zach, You mentioned a word syndicate, like imagine, maybe I don't have that much money, but I have less money. How did that manifest itself in the reporting and where did that take you guys?
turns.zh: 好，我们说到可能有几百万美元的规模，也可能是一个持有超过 5 亿美元的家族在做这件事。Zach，你提到一个词——辛迪加。设想一下，也许我没有那么多钱，只有比较少的钱。这种情况在你们的报道中是怎么呈现的？它又把你们引向了哪里？

turns.en: Yeah, so a lot of these three fifty ones are a money manager or somebody like that will go around to a bunch of their clients and say, hey, if you've got a million bucks and you want to get the advantage of this, you can put it in this pot and we'll kind of gather them all up and we'll create one ETF. So that kind of spreads the you know, the cost, the kind of administrative cost of setting thing up over a larger number of people.
turns.zh: 是的，很多这类 351 是这样运作的：一位资产管理人或者类似角色会去接触自己的一批客户，说：嘿，如果你有 100 万美元、又想享受这个好处，就把钱放进这个池子里，我们把大家凑到一起，设立一只 ETF。这样一来，设立过程中的成本、那种行政管理成本，就被分摊到更多人身上。

turns.en: And is it clear yet how common that is versus maybe like one benefactor or one source of the seed money.
turns.zh: 现在能弄清楚这种做法有多普遍吗？相比只有一位出资人、或者种子资金只有一个来源的情况。

turns.en: I'm not sure we have a strong view. I think it looks like probably most of them are some kind of they're either syndicated or they're maybe from a private fund where we assume there's probably multiple investors, and then there's only been a couple I think where it really looks like it's probably just one or two people.
turns.zh: 我不确定我们有明确的判断。看起来大多数要么是辛迪加式的，要么来自一只私募基金——我们推测那里面应该有多位投资者。真正看起来可能只有一两个人的，我想只有几只。

turns.en: And we've seen more and more financial advisors get involved into this, and obviously they construct relatively like maybe similar portfolios for their clients, so it makes sense that some of those will be pulled. And like, if you and me both have exposures to Magnificent seven, maybe we can combine our assets and do something like that. But I would say, yeah, like many of them are syndicated.
turns.zh: 而且我们看到越来越多的财务顾问参与其中。显然，他们为客户构建的组合往往比较相似，所以其中一些被合并起来是说得通的。比如说，如果你和我都有 Magnificent Seven 的敞口，也许我们可以把资产合起来做这样一件事。但我会说，是的，其中很多都是辛迪加式的。

turns.en: I want to talk about one of the pushbacks here to the article, and I brought this up on etfi Q with Zach because it's good for to like kind of unpack this. So you know, everybody likes that ETFs democratize things, right, even this particular administration is trying to democratize privates and all kinds of things. They want the little guy to have the same access. One of the pushbacks here is, hey, look this, this exchange fund concept has been going on in the very ultra rich world of private banking for a long time, and they did the same thing. It's just the top point one percent or like the ultra ultra rich. Now it's becoming democratized, where like, okay, maybe people a little less ultra rich. But I think Schwab might even be having some participation in this, which means even regular retail could participate. Isn't that good? Like, in other words, shouldn't everybody have access to this tax quote dodge or should all of it be shut down? Because I don't recall seeing a lot on like the exchange funds concept. It's like, I know, once it gets in ETF, it sort of becomes like mainstreamed and like it's like easy to find and track and look for. But the private banking world I believe has been doing this.
turns.zh: 我想谈谈外界对这篇报道的一个反驳，我在 ETF IQ 上也跟 Zach 提过，因为值得把它拆开来看。大家都知道喜欢 ETF 让很多事情变得平民化，对吧？连这一届政府也在试图让私募市场等各种东西平民化，他们希望小人物能获得同样的准入。这里的一个反驳是：嘿，看，交换基金这个概念在超级富豪的私人银行世界里已经存在很长时间了，他们做的是同样的事，只不过服务于顶端 0.1%、也就是超级超级富豪。而现在它正在变得平民化——好吧，也许是没有那么超级富豪的人也能参与了。我想 Schwab 甚至也在参与进来，这意味着连普通散户都能参与。这难道不是好事吗？换句话说，是不是每个人都应该能用上这种所谓的避税手段，还是说应该把它全部叫停？因为我不记得看到过多少关于交换基金这个概念的报道。就像我知道的那样，一旦它变成 ETF，就有点被主流化了，很容易查找、追踪和检索。但我相信私人银行界已经这么做好一阵子了。

turns.en: For a while. Yeah, I mean yeah, So the earlier iteration of this idea was the exchange fund, which, to your point, I think eric is truitionally seen as pretty expensive. It would be like Goldman Sachs or Morgan Stanley would go around and try to round up money into one of these, and the concept there was similar. You got a bunch of rich people. Let's say I'm some guy who I'm in a former executive at an industrial company, so I've got a ton of stock in this one company, and you're a former executive at a tech company. You've got a ton of stock in that company. So we find a bunch of these people who have kind of diverse a group that's diversed but everyone's very concentrated. You put all your money into one big partnership, or put all your stock into one big partnership, nobody sells anything. But now suddenly I've got a much more diversified exposure. So the difference with the three point fifty one that take makes it like way more powerful in a certain way, in addition to being probably lower fees and access to more people, is that the ETF can go out and get rid of those stocks and bring in other ones.
turns.zh: 有一阵子了。是的，我是说，对，这个想法更早的版本就是交换基金。就像你说的，Eric，它传统上被认为相当昂贵。通常是 Goldman Sachs 或 Morgan Stanley 出面去四处募集资金，凑成这样一个基金，概念是类似的：找来一群富人。比如我是某家工业公司的前高管，所以手里有一大堆这家公司的股票；而你是一家科技公司的前高管，手里有一大堆那家公司的股票。于是我们找来一堆这样的人——这个群体彼此之间是分散的，但每个人自己都非常集中——你把所有的钱，或者说所有的股票，放进一个大的合伙实体里，没有人卖出任何东西，但突然间我的敞口就变得分散多了。所以 351 带来的区别，让它在某种意义上强大得多——除了费用可能更低、能覆盖更多人之外——就在于这只 ETF 可以主动把那些股票处理掉，再换入其他股票。

turns.en: We currently identified one hundred and five ETFs and the assets under management are more than twenty billion, So you can do the math of how big is the average three fifty one conversion. It is indeed the case that if you go to those platform that offer it, often the minimums are a few hundred thousand, which obviously it's very accessible to retail investor. But what we've seen so far is that a lot of the people using them are indeed in kind of a higher income bracket than someone who would contribute hundred thousand. And another point I want to make is that our story focuses on people like We mentioned the Mirage family, we mentioned Rory Riggs, we mentioned Gay Plotkin, these are all people who have potentially easy access to the big banks and can put their money into exchange funds and all the fancy private asset products. But clearly they're choosing this very transparent platform like ETF. Filing has so much information you can find all of that. So if all those people are using that type of vehicle to convert their assets, perhaps their benefits are a little bit better or at least in certain cases than what the banks can offer you.
turns.zh: 我们目前识别出 105 只这样的 ETF，管理资产规模超过 200 亿美元，所以你可以算一下平均一笔 351 转换有多大。确实，如果你去看那些提供这项服务的平台，最低门槛常常是几十万美元，这对散户投资者来说显然很容易触及。但我们目前看到的是，很多使用它的人，收入层级确实高于那种只会投入 10 万美元的人。我想说的另一点是，我们的报道聚焦于这样一些人：我们提到了 Merage 家族，提到了 Rory Riggs，提到了 Gabe Plotkin。这些人本来都可以轻松接触大银行，可以把钱放进交换基金和各种花哨的私人资产产品。但他们显然选择了 ETF 这种非常透明的平台——ETF 的备案文件里有大量信息，你都能查到。所以如果这些人都用这种工具来转换资产，也许它的好处比银行能提供的要更好一些，至少在某些情况下是这样。

turns.en: And then I think, you know, another pushback here, not a pushback, but it's more just like and I think Joel kind of hit it with the first question was basically like, if you're a fiduciary, whether an asset manager or an advisor, tax alpha is your job. You know, you're you know, there's programs of software that help you do tax loss harvesting and whatnot. And people go in and out of stocks and ETFs. In December, we see a ton of flows into spy because people are going to hide out there for a month and then leave in a month later, and that's tax loss harvest thing. I guess just give us the if that's your fiduciary job, and obviously you're just going to push that until the government tells you no. And so I guess let's just start there, which is that, Okay, fine, this is a something that's happening. All of the advisors and asset men just trying to help their clients, which is their job. But it's getting to a point where it's like questionable whether it's breaking the spirit of the tax code. Where does the government stand on this in terms of the Treasury and the irs.
turns.zh: 然后我觉得，另一个反驳——也不算反驳，更像是 Joe 在第一个问题里点到的那点：如果你是受托人，无论是资产管理人还是投顾，做 tax alpha 就是你的工作。你知道，有各种软件程序帮你做税务亏损收割（tax-loss harvesting）之类的事情，人们进出股票和 ETF。12 月我们会看到大量资金流入 SPY，因为大家要去那里躲一个月，一个月后再离开，那就是税务亏损收割。所以如果这是你的受托职责，你显然会一直往前推，直到政府告诉你不行。那我们就从这里说起：好吧，这件事正在发生，所有投顾和资产管理人只是在帮他们的客户，这是他们的职责。但它已经到了一个地步，让人怀疑是否违背了税法的精神。就 Treasury 和 IRS 而言，政府在这件事上的立场是什么？

turns.en: That's a great question. And Denisa and I were at a conference just the other day where we heard from the two people who are kind of making that decision. There's two Treasury officials who were sort of giving a talk to Wall Street lawyers about where do we stand on these newfangled tax alpha concepts, And one of them that they spend a lot of time talking about was three fifty ones, and they pretty much, I'd say, it's fair to say, Denisa, they made it clear that they're not trying to attack all three fifty ones exactly, but they don't like some of the more aggressive moves. And what they talked about specifically was sort of three fifty one ETFs and within that they were saying, and I remember remembering this now, they said they were concerned about people contributing assets with an intent to get rid of them, or assets that didn't really fit with the mission, the stated mission of the three fifty one. So there's a lot of stuff in the tax code that basically says, yeah, sure you can do a three fifty one, but it shouldn't be an attempt to achieve diversification. Now, all that we've been talking about this whole episode has been using a three fifty one to achieve diversification. So it's kind of like a fine line here, but suffice to say, Treasury has seen stuff that they think is probably going too far.
turns.zh: 这是个很好的问题。就在前几天，Deniza 和我参加了一个会议，听到了基本上正在做这个决定的两个人讲话。有两位 Treasury 官员在对华尔街律师做一场演讲，主题是：对于这些新奇的 tax alpha 概念，我们的立场是什么。他们花了大量时间谈的一个话题就是 351。我可以说——Deniza，这么说应该公平——他们明确表示，他们并不是要打击所有的 351，但他们不喜欢其中一些更激进的做法。他们具体谈的是 351 ETF，而在其中——我现在想起来了——他们说，他们担心有人投入资产的本意就是要把这些资产甩掉，或者投入的资产与 351 的既定宗旨并不真正相符。税法里有很多条款基本上是在说：是的，当然你可以做 351，但它不应该是一种试图实现分散化的安排。而我们这一整期节目谈的，全都是用 351 来实现分散化。所以这里是一条很细的界线，但可以说，Treasury 已经看到了一些他们认为可能走得太远的东西。

turns.en: Just on this achieved diversification. We had Brent Sullivan, I call him the tax man. He is the tax taxing everything. You should go to his LinkedIn or Twitter his next level. Anyway, he said this achieved diversification. I didn't totally realize this, but maybe I interpret him wrong. He says that wasn't the spirit of the code, Like you shouldn't be using it to achieve diversification. But isn't that what almost all these are doing? Like wouldn't they all be suspect if that's.
turns.zh: 就『实现分散化』这一点。我们之前请过 Brent Sullivan——我叫他税务先生，他对什么都要征税。你应该去看看他的 LinkedIn 或 Twitter，简直是另一个层次。总之，他说到这个实现分散化——我之前没完全意识到这一点，但也许我理解错了他的意思——他说这不符合税法的本意，也就是说你不应该用它来实现分散化。可几乎所有这些交易做的不就是这件事吗？如果是这样，那它们不都成了可疑对象？

turns.en: The exactly I mean, I think what happened here is a couple of times policymakers said, well, we don't like this achieving diversification thing. We're going to write out these rules that kind of prevent what we think is the problem. And of course tax layers looked at those rules as like, okay, well here here are the rules of the game. How can we gain them? And so, yeah, thanks for the signposts exactly, and like let's go right up to that line and then maybe use some other tricks you didn't think about to even kind of go beyond that. And so, for instance, there's a rule like I think one position can't be more than twenty five, right, and then maybe the overall number of positions has to be I think at least eleven. So there's all these rules of like how to how they define diversified. Well, you can do a lot with that, particularly for instance, if you borrow money to add some other stuff into the pot before you do it, right, So there's a lot of tricks you can play that really achieved the goal diversification without running a foul of the black letter of the law.
turns.zh: 没错。我是说，我认为这里发生的事情是：政策制定者有几次说，好吧，我们不喜欢这种实现分散化的做法，我们要写出一些规则来防止我们认为的问题。而税务律师们看着这些规则想：好，那这就是游戏规则，我们怎么才能钻空子？于是——是啊，谢谢你们竖起的路标——那我们就一直走到那条线跟前，然后再用一些你们没想到的其他技巧，甚至越过那条线。比如说，有一条规则我记得是单一持仓不能超过 25%，对吧？然后持仓总数我记得至少要 11 个。所以有一整套关于如何定义分散化的规则。嗯，这里面可做的文章很多，特别是如果你在操作之前先借钱往池子里塞一些其他资产的话。所以有很多技巧可以玩，能真正实现分散化的目标，却不违反法律条文的字面规定。

turns.en: And so if someone was going to maybe change the rules, would that end up looking like and where would that come from? Would it be from Treasury?
turns.zh: 那么，如果有人要修改规则，最终会是什么样子？会从哪里出台？是 Treasury 吗？

turns.en: I just wanted to say that for the Treasury is like really those things that are pushing the rules. And the thing that Zach mentioned is stuffing is the fact that investors borrow money to kind of sidetrack those diversification rules. There is also sequential seating, which you're using a couple of ETFs to do that. So just generally the versification rule, I guess was fine with the Treasury as long as people don't push the boundaries and become extra creative to surpass it. And when it comes to what the Treasury can do is something we've been covering for a long time. The conversation about this started at the start of the year, at least as far as we know, is that they've been talking about issuing Guydance. So the main and kind of the thing that a lot of people in the industry worried about is labeling this transaction of interest, which will be then heavily reviewed by the IRS. And obviously it's kind of a name you put for transaction that could potentially be tax avoidance or some type of tax dodge. So every time Treasure officials review IRS officials review the filings. They're like, oh, we have to double check this because clearly it is problematic. Of course, that's kind of the most severe measure they could take, and we're not sure if that's something they said everything that was on the table. We're looking at all those measures, but there could be different measures that stop that. The parts of the transaction they're worried about, and they're worried about people changing the holdings too fast. We have reporting about people changing the in the first few days. They're worried about people changing too many of the of the initial holdings. We have reporting about that. But that said, many many of the three fifty one conversions don't break those rules. So I guess the ideal thing for the treasure in the industry is to kind of stop those bad try score to prossings who are trying to avoid those rules and changing that, and maybe that could be done through guidance. And I guess that's the agreement now that if something is then is going to be gind us like, it's not like Congress will pass actual legislation to change this.
turns.zh: 我想先说的是，对 Treasury 而言，真正成问题的是那些在推挤规则边界的做法。Zach 提到的 stuffing（资产填塞）就是投资者借钱来绕过分散化规则。还有一种叫 sequential seeding（分步注入种子资金），你会用几只 ETF 来做这件事。所以总体来说，我猜 Treasury 对分散化规则本身是没意见的，只要大家不去推挤边界、不要变得格外有创意以规避它。至于 Treasury 能做什么，这是我们跟踪报道了很久的事。据我们所知，相关讨论至少从年初就开始了：他们一直在讨论发布指引（guidance）。其中业内很多人最担心的主要一点，就是把这类交易标记为关注交易（transaction of interest），一旦被这样标记，就会受到 IRS 的重点审查。显然，这个名称是给那些可能构成避税或某种避税手段的交易贴上的标签。所以每次 Treasury 官员、IRS 官员审查备案文件时，他们就会说：哦，这个我们得仔细核对，因为它显然有问题。当然，这是他们能采取的最严厉的措施，我们也不确定他们是否说过所有选项都在考虑范围内——他们说在审视所有这些措施。但也可能有不同的措施，去阻止他们担心的那些交易环节。他们担心人们换持仓换得太快——我们有报道说有人在头几天就换掉了持仓；他们担心人们换掉太多初始持仓——这一点我们也有报道。话虽如此，非常多的 351 转换并没有违反那些规则。所以我想，对 Treasury 和行业来说理想的结果，是阻止那些试图规避规则、乱改持仓的坏行为者，而这也许可以通过指引来实现。我想现在的共识是，如果要出台什么，那会是指引，而不是国会通过真正的立法来改变这一点。

turns.en: Yeah, Congress can fascinate Yah, Yeah, I love these three words transactions of interest that just is like such a great catch all for how they think about this.
turns.zh: 是啊，国会那边就很有意思了。耶，对，我很喜欢 transactions of interest（关注交易）这三个词，它真是个绝妙的万能标签，正好装下他们对这件事的想法。

turns.en: One thing about this just taking a big step back. I sometimes grapple with this because on one hand, I'm like, you know, ETFs, probably the investors who use ETFs trade a lot, Like we're talking seventy trillion dollars in volume a year. There's a lot of capital gains being triggered there, that's being paid. They probably pay a lot of taxes. I think capital gains are like ten percent of tax income for the government, so it's a pretty good amount. And I'm like, you know, this is just part of what people do, and you can't avoid it unless you die. Like when you die, then all your tax liabilities are gone and your kids don't have to pay them, but you're dead. So it's not like, you know, some people are using that like like that's your way out of it. Like that's a pretty dark, like dark kind of concept there that Okay, yeah, fine, don't have to pay taxes if you pass away, But does anybody really want to do that anyway. I do think that the bigger picture here is the stock market has been such a massive source of wealth and of the wealth gap that the top one percent own half of the stock market now and they've gotten like fabulously rich. And then because we've been covering Trump accounts, are trying to get the other fifty percent of Americans in the stock market because they've been left behind of all these exorbitant gains. And so I do kind of understand, I think from a holistic point of view, like, hey, look, you made a ton of money. Just sell this the damn stock and pay the taxes. Like you're going to get money too. It's not like they're going to take all the money. And the gun then would take that money and do something with it in the government. Right, So that's the issue here is that even if you do pay it later, the government could have taken that money and done something with it immediately, whereas you take it and you're able to compound and earn even more. So that that's really the problem here, right. It's more just a because I was at the Bogel Heads conference and this guy he made a good point, is like, listen, just pay your taxes, like you know, it's not like all of the money you have a gain. So that's good. Bogel said the same thing. He was like, if you have to pay capital gains, that's good. It means you made money. Is there a philosophical thing going on here too?
turns.zh: 退一大步来看这件事，我有时自己也在纠结：一方面，你知道，ETF——用 ETF 的投资者交易很频繁，我们说的是一年 70 万亿美元的成交量。那里触发了大量资本利得，而且这些税是实实在在缴了的，他们大概缴了很多税。我想资本利得大约占政府税收收入的 10%，所以是相当可观的一笔。我会想，这就是人们在做的事的一部分，你没法避免，除非你去世。人去世了，所有税务责任就消失了，你的孩子也不用缴，但你自己死了。所以也不是说——有些人确实在用这一条，那是你的出路。这其实是个挺黑暗的概念：好吧，是的，人走了就不用交税了。但反正有谁真的想这么做吗？我确实认为，更大的图景是：股市一直是财富以及财富差距的巨大来源，如今最富的 1% 拥有股市的一半，他们变得极其富有。另一方面，因为我们一直在报道 Trump accounts（特朗普账户），政府正试图让另外 50% 的美国人进入股市，因为这些惊人的涨幅把他们落在了后面。所以我多少能理解，从整体角度看：嘿，你赚了一大笔钱，就把那该死的股票卖了、把税交了。你自己也还能留下钱，政府不会把你的钱全拿走，然后政府可以拿这笔钱去做点事。对吧？所以问题就在这里：即便你以后再缴这笔税，政府本来可以立刻拿到那笔钱并派上用场，而你把钱留在手里，还能继续复利、赚得更多。这才是真正的问题所在。这更多是——因为我在 Bogleheads 大会上，有个人提出了一个很好的观点：听着，就把税交了吧。并不是所有的钱都要交掉，你还有收益留下来，这是好事。Bogle 也说过同样的话：如果你必须缴资本利得税，那是好事，说明你赚到钱了。这里面是不是也有一种理念层面的东西在起作用？

turns.en: I think it's kind of a game, right, which is how do I see if I can try something and maybe pay less? And that to me is like Wall Street loves a good game and that is the game, and there's experts for that game, and if you can find them and figure out something like, see if you can do it.
turns.zh: 我觉得这有点像一场游戏，对吧？就是看能不能试点什么办法，也许少缴一点。对我来说，华尔街最喜欢一场好游戏，而这正是那场游戏，而且这个游戏有专家。如果你能找到他们、想出点什么办法，那就试试看能不能做成。

turns.en: I mean, there are many layers to this, but generally we know that financial advisors have been struggling to kind of justify fees for a very long time. Deriveing alpha that's better than the market than buying s and P five hundred front has not been easy. So there is an element of that where financial advisors have really been selling tax ALFA and it's become this thing where it's just like, oh, this is where you need really need us and people, you know, people are worried about taxes. I tell you about taxes and you suddenly get very interesting. So there is that aspect of that, and also a lot of those approaches, as much as they could be available as low as fifty hundred thousand, they're actually effective if you are high network individual. We've talked a lot about the democratization of those, but often the benefits at a very low kind of investment level are not that big. The point where you generate those benefits is where the numbers get serious and we get like kind of a six figure above eight figure and above to actually get the benefits. And the thing that really really complicated this debate is that a lot of those companies are very aggressive with advertising, and even the Treasury this is something we mentioned, they said, we saw an ad that you can save three hundred thousand in taxes on one million investment. And I think this is where the boundary of like, oh, it's our fuduciary duty to maximize your tax saving. It's our re fuducary duty to do all of that. But where it got complicated is that we got very smart about tax optimization, about tax planning and tax engineering, but people also advertise it in the wrong ways. Like some firms are like, oh, we're saying, oh, it's tax self, we're working on your returns. But some firms are really pushing the boundaries with advertisement, and I think that's where it draws public backlash and clearly regulators are not excited about it.
turns.zh: 这件事有很多层面。但我们大致知道，财务顾问长期以来一直在为证明自己收费的合理性而挣扎。想要获得跑赢市场、跑赢买 S&P 500 基金的阿尔法并不容易。所以其中有这样一个成分：财务顾问真正在卖的是 tax alpha，它变成了一种说法——哦，这正是你真正需要我们的地方。而人们确实担心税收，你只要跟他们谈税，你突然就变得非常有吸引力。所以确实有这个层面。另外，很多这类策略虽然门槛可以低到 5 万、10 万美元，但真正有效的前提是你属于高净值个人。我们谈了很多这类策略的平民化，但在很低的投资金额上，好处往往并没有那么大。真正产生这些好处的临界点，是当数字变得可观的时候——要到七位数甚至八位数以上，才能实实在在拿到好处。而真正让这场辩论变得复杂的是，很多这类公司的广告非常激进。连 Treasury 也提到过这一点——他们说：我们看到一则广告，宣称 100 万美元的投资可以省下 30 万美元的税。我想这就是边界所在：一边是『最大化你的节税额是我们的受托责任，做这些全都是我们的受托责任』；但事情变得复杂的地方在于，我们在税务优化、税务规划和税务工程方面变得非常精明，可人们在宣传这些的时候用了错误的方式。有些公司说的是：哦，我们说的是节税，我们在帮你处理回报。但有些公司在广告上真的在推挤边界，我认为这正是引发公众反弹的地方，而且监管机构显然对此不乐见。
